title: He held the money…
paragraphs:
He held the money…
but lost his soul.
And that should disturb you more than you think.
Because Judas didn’t look like a villain.
He looked like a follower.

He walked where Jesus walked.
He heard what others only dreamed of hearing.
He was trusted enough to carry the group’s finances.
But something was off.
And it didn’t show… at first.
That’s the danger.

Not loud rebellion.
Hidden misalignment.

A heart that says, “I’m with Jesus”—
but only as long as it benefits me.
Let’s go deeper.

Judas wasn’t just greedy.
He was disappointed.
Some scholars interpret that Judas expected a political Messiah—someone who would overthrow Rome, elevate Israel, and possibly elevate him. Power. Influence. Control.

But Jesus kept talking about surrender.
About dying to self.
About a Kingdom not of this world.

And slowly… quietly…
Judas’ expectations started to rot into resentment.
Have you ever been there?

You prayed—but God didn’t answer the way you wanted.
You followed—but life got harder, not easier.
You served—but no recognition came.
And deep inside, something whispered:
“Is Jesus still worth it… if He doesn’t give me what I want?”
That’s where betrayal begins.
Not with thirty pieces of silver.
But with a divided heart.
Scripture doesn’t hide it.
“Then Satan entered into Judas called Iscariot… He went away and conferred with the chief priests… and they were glad, and agreed to give him money.” (Luke 22:3–5)
Notice the progression.

Opened door.
Dark influence.
Private decision.
Public betrayal.

Sin rarely explodes overnight.
It seeps in… quietly… convincingly.
And here’s the chilling part:

Judas was so close to Jesus…
and still completely lost.

Jesus Himself said,
“Did I not choose you, the Twelve? And yet one of you is a devil.” (John 6:70)
That’s not poetic language.
That’s a warning.

You can be around holy things—
and still be ruled by unholy desires.

You can raise your hands in worship—
and still be negotiating with sin in secret.

You can say “Lord, Lord”—
and still refuse to let Him be Lord.

And that tension… that hidden compromise…
will eventually demand a decision.
Judas made his.
“For what will you give me if I deliver Him to you?” (Matthew 26:15)
Pause.
That question is still echoing today.
What will you trade Jesus for?

Approval?
Comfort?
A relationship?
A hidden addiction?
A secret ambition no one knows about?

Because whatever you refuse to surrender…
you will eventually choose over Him.
And here’s what breaks the heart.
Judas didn’t just betray Jesus.
He kissed Him.
“Now the betrayer had given them a sign, saying, ‘The one I will kiss is the man; seize Him.’ And he came up to Jesus at once and said, ‘Greetings, Rabbi!’ And he kissed Him.” (Matthew 26:48–49)

Affection on the outside.
Rebellion on the inside.
That’s the most dangerous kind of faith.

Performative.
Polished.
But powerless.
But don’t miss this—
Jesus knew.
From the beginning… He knew.
“And yet… He still washed Judas’ feet.” (John 13:5, 11)
Let that wreck you.

The Savior kneeling before His betrayer.
Grace extended to a man already planning to reject it.
Why?
Because that’s who Jesus is.

Not just holy.
Merciful.

Not just just.
Compassionate.
But here’s where the story splits.
Peter failed too.

He denied Jesus three times.
Swore he didn’t know Him.
But Peter wept… and returned.
Judas felt remorse… but ran away.
“Then when Judas, his betrayer, saw that Jesus was condemned, he changed his mind… and returned the thirty pieces of silver… saying, ‘I have sinned by betraying innocent blood.’” (Matthew 27:3–4)
He admitted sin.
But he didn’t run to Jesus.
He ran from Him.
That’s the difference between condemnation and conviction.

Condemnation says:
“You’ve gone too far.”

Conviction says:
“Come back.”
Judas believed his sin was greater than God’s mercy.
And that lie… destroyed him.
Friend, hear this clearly:
No sin you carry is greater than the cross of Christ.
Jesus didn’t just die for the faithful.

He died for the fake.
The struggling.
The double-minded.
The ones who showed up outwardly but were breaking inwardly.
“For our sake He made Him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.” (2 Corinthians 5:21)
That includes you.
Yes—you.

The one hiding.
The one pretending.
The one negotiating with sin while still trying to follow Jesus.
Grace is not for perfect people.
Grace is for surrendered people.

Are you following Jesus…
or using Him?

Are you surrendered…
or just surrounding yourself with spiritual things?

Are you Peter—broken but coming back?
Or Judas—remorseful but running away?
Today… you choose.

Not tomorrow.
Not when life is easier.
Now.
Turn your heart fully to Christ.

No more half-following.
No more secret deals.
No more divided loyalty.
Repent.
That word simply means: change direction.

Stop running from Him.
Run to Him.

Because the same Jesus who was betrayed…
is the same Jesus who still saves.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” (1 John 1:9)
Not some sin.
All.
Not partial cleansing.
Complete.
This is your moment.

Drop the silver.
Choose the Savior.
If this hit your heart, don’t ignore it.
